text:
Sam: Hey folks 3 day 1 here. Trying to build the runtime from source on my Fedora 38 laptop using the standard dev container. Build fails with a mix of ptxas/driver errors and a GLIBCXX symbol error. Anyone seen this combo?

Sam: short excerpt:
```bash
[ 23%] Linking CXX executable llm_server
ptxas fatal   : Value 'sm_86' is not valid for option 'gpu-name'
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lnvidia-ml
/usr/bin/ld: /opt/third_party/libtorch/lib/libtorch.so: undefined symbol: _ZNSt7__cxx1112basic_stringIcSt11char_traitsIcESaIcEE6assignERKS4_
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Sam: I'm running `docker run --gpus all -v $(pwd):/src -w /src redwood/dev:cuda-12.2 make -j12` and I did not intentionally mount any host /usr libs.

Mika: welcome! :tada: quick checklist: `nvidia-smi` on host, `nvcc --version` in container, and `strings /usr/lib64/libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBCXX` inside the container for the GLIBCXX list. The GLIBCXX undefined symbol means the prebuilt libtorch needs a different libstdc++ than what's available in the container.

Natanael: +1. Also double-check you're not using podman rootless or some bind that sneaks host libs in. The `-lnvidia-ml` at link means the build wants NVML headers/libs at compile time; we made that optional in CMake recently but some branches still link it. For the ptxas line: verify CUDA_ARCH env or hardcoded arch in CMake (grep for sm_86/sm_90).

Rosie: Fedora sometimes ships a newer libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30+ that doesn't match our prebuilt third_party artifacts (we build them on Ubuntu images). If you can't rebuild libtorch locally, use the dev image matching the binary's distro (we keep ubuntu-based images). Also check `dmesg` for module signature failures 3 if Secure Boot blocked DKMS modules you won't have /dev/nvidia* inside the container which can cause `-lnvidia-ml`/`-lcuda` problems.

Sam: running checks: host `nvidia-smi` shows Driver Version: 535.54, GPU is 3070. Inside container `nvcc --version` -> CUDA 12.2. `dmesg` shows "nvidia_drm: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing".

Mika: signature failure -> Secure Boot / unsigned DKMS module. If you can turn off Secure Boot that's fastest; otherwise infra can sign and enroll modules for company laptops. That explains some of the missing device files. However GLIBCXX mismatch is separate (third_party vs container distro).

Natanael: for immediate unblock: 1) try `redwood/dev:cuda-11.8` which tends to be friendlier for older host setups; 2) copy the repo into the container FS (avoid mounting from /home or odd FS) and rebuild; 3) if libtorch is the problem, rebuild the third_party artifact inside the container (`scripts/build_third_party.sh`) so it links against the exact libstdc++ version.

Rosie: also confirm Docker uses nvidia-container-toolkit on Fedora (we've seen folks accidentally use an older runtime). `docker info | grep -i nvidia` and `nvidia-container-cli info` are good quick checks.

Sam: tried switching to `redwood/dev:cuda-11.8` and copied repo into container FS. Rebuilt third_party/libtorch via the script and the GLIBCXX error went away. Still had to remove a hardcoded sm_90 I found in cmake/cuda_flags.cmake and set `export CUDAARCHS=sm_86`. After that the link completed and binary runs.

Mika: sweet 3 sounds like two separate issues (Secure Boot driver module + third_party ABI mismatch). Can you add the Fedora 38 + kernel + driver combo to the onboarding doc so we can include a note about distro ABI differences?

Sam: will do. Also filing a small GH PR to make NVML optional in that telemetry plugin so we don't require libnvidia-ml at link time.

infra-bot: INFRA-590 opened: "Sign DKMS modules for Secure Boot laptops + add Fedora notes to dev-image compatibility matrix". Assigned to infra.

Sam: thanks all, appreciate the quick help. Tagging @Mika @Natanael if I need a review on the PR. :thumbsup:
